works.abstract: Climate models predict that Southern California will begin experiencing longer periods of drought and more intense storms in the coming decades. Long periods of drought have the potential to allow for the buildup of pollutants on undisturbed areas, such as the roofs of buildings and in gutters. When the rain does fall, these hazardous materials can be mobilized by the stormwater and impact human health and the environment, as well as leach into groundwater, which is especially dangerous when the water table is low. Despite this, cities such as Los Angeles have very little stormwater monitoring. In order to benchmark possible stormwater contaminant levels, stormwater runoff was collected from four locations on the University Park Campus of the University of Southern California in Downtown Los Angeles during seven different storms spanning from 2021 to 2023. Major dissolved elements were measured by Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). Solid particulate matter was filtered out of stormwater and examined by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). Dissolved Ca, Na, S, K, and Mg were found in the highest concentrations, while the most abundant elements with potential hazards to humans were Mg and Zn. A parking structure was found to have the highest total dissolved elemental mass, but when normalized for roof area, the highest elemental concentrations were found in buildings closest to the nearest freeway. Under SEM, samples contained abundant near-spherical particles below the size of 10 µm, which is small enough to be embedded in human lungs. High levels of zinc in the samples can be attributed to Tire Wear Particles, and the near-spherical particles are most likely soot from incomplete combustion in diesel engines. These results reveal that distance from the freeway, and not any other potential driver, is the main control on the amount of elemental loading. The main source of pollution is mobile combustion, which is non-point in nature. The results of this study call attention to the need for more robust stormwater monitoring systems, especially in areas bound by heavily trafficked roadways.
works.title: Stormwater Runoff from the University of Southern California, University Park Campus: Potential Hazards and Drivers of Dissolved and Particulate Pollution
